label: Bayesian likelihood contrast determines binary check accuracy gain
paraphrase: For a fixed binary target with nondegenerate prior p, a binary check with likelihoods a,b and nondegenerate predictive weight w, and conditional posteriors u,v satisfying the coherent joint equations, the pooled prior is p, w(1-w) times the binary-check accuracy gain equals the square of p(1-p)(a-b), and the gain is zero exactly when a=b. All likelihoods and posteriors are in [0,1]. The result describes expected accuracy gain, not actual calibration or an obligation to investigate.
